introduction: On this Sunday, Zechariah announces a king who comes humbly, riding on a donkey, bringing peace to the nations. In the Gospel, Jesus thanks his Father for revealing the Kingdom to little ones, and invites all who are weary: Come to me, and I will give you rest; my yoke is easy and my burden light. Paul tells us to live by the Spirit. Let us come to Jesus and find rest.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is gracious and merciful, slow to anger and rich in love. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may be humble and gentle like her Lord, bringing peace to the nations. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the weary and the overburdened: that they may come to Jesus and find rest. Let us pray to the Lord.
For children and all the little ones of the world: that they may be loved and protected. Let us pray to the Lord.
For leaders of nations: that they may choose the way of peace rather than the way of war. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may learn from Jesus, who is gentle and humble of heart. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord Jesus, you invite the weary to come to you and find rest. Teach us to be gentle and humble like you, and to share your yoke with joy. You live and reign for ever and ever.

reflection.title: Learn from me
reflection.body:
Zechariah describes a surprising king: "Behold, your King comes to you! He is righteous, and having salvation; lowly, and riding on a donkey." He does not come on a war horse. He removes the chariots and the battle bows, "and he will speak peace to the nations." The Gospels see this prophecy fulfilled when Jesus enters Jerusalem on Palm Sunday.

In the Gospel, Jesus prays aloud to his Father: "I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you hid these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to infants." God's Kingdom is not grasped by cleverness but received by the humble and childlike.

Then Jesus speaks some of the most consoling words in the Gospels: "Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest." Many people today are weary: overworked, anxious, carrying burdens of grief, illness or guilt. Jesus invites all of them.

He does not promise a life without any burden. He offers his yoke: "Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart." A yoke is shared; Jesus walks beside us and carries the weight with us. "For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light." What makes it light is his presence and his love.

Paul tells us how to live this new life: not "after the flesh," driven by selfish desires, but by the Spirit. "For if you live after the flesh, you must die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live."

This week, name the burdens you are carrying, and bring each one to Jesus in prayer. Accept his invitation to rest. And try to be gentle and humble with others, as he is with you.
